repairs.component: Legacy server event bus entry point
repairs.before: Expanded real Redis test delivered three unique events to each package subscriber and zero to the actual legacy server subscriber.
repairs.after: The legacy entry point re-exports the shared process-wide bus, removing the separate consumer implementation. Package copies and legacy import deliver identical event IDs; close/reopen monitoring remains correct.

repairs.before: Actual registration functions with equal bundled handler names delivered the calendar sync effect once and omitted search indexing.
repairs.after: Stable explicit subscriber IDs preserve both effects independently. The regression executes real registration and handler functions through Redis; external calendar service and search persistence are controlled effect probes.

limits: The previous package-only delivery test did not cover the legacy server implementation; this evidence supersedes its broad delivery claim.
Production browser validation must use a new candidate containing this repair. Current native af96daf0 does not contain it.
Other subscriber families and cross-process consumer fanout are not proven by the calendar/search identity regression.
